significant_events.title: Mali: HRW confirms the execution of Malian soldiers by Jnim and the death of civilians killed by the army
significant_events.summary: In a new report published on Monday, October 19, the human rights organization claims that the Support Group for Islam and Muslims (Jnim) confirmed to it summary executions of Malian soldiers in Tabrichat, in the Gao region, following the attack on a military convoy from Anefis, last July The NGO Human Rights Watch (HRW) also accuses the Malian army and the Russian Africa Corps of having killed and wounded several dozen civilians during recent military operations.

The “Night of the Popular Progressive Revolution” brought together thousands of residents on 30 September on the Place de la Résistance in Ouagadougou.

Mali.title: Sikasso: a thwarted attack at the Mamassoni checkpoint
Mali.summary: An attack on the Mamassoni checkpoint in Sikasso was thwarted on the night of Sunday, October 18, 2026, around 9 p.m., according to local reports. The reaction of the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) would have forced the attackers to abandon their plan. The situation was quickly brought under control, according to the same sources A statement from security authorities is expected to provide more details on the circumstances of the incident.

Mali.title: Mali’s military and armed groups committing abuses against civilians: HRW
Mali.summary: Mali’s military and its Russian paramilitary allies have killed civilians in breach of international law, and opposition armed groups have done likewise, Human Rights Watch (HRW) says. Soldiers and fighters “are committing grave laws-of-war violations while international organisations and governments largely stand by”, the United States-based rights watchdog said in a report released on Monday.

Mali.title: In Mali, mining companies caught between fiscal vice and logistical headache
Mali.summary: In Mali, mining companies caught between fiscal stranglehold and logistical headache Faced with rising royalties, deteriorating security conditions or legal disputes with the ruling junta, mining companies navigate an increasingly uncertain environment Burned-out tanker trucks, blocked roads, besieged gas stations… After a particularly turbulent 2025, the numerous blockades imposed in the first half of 2026 by the Group for the Support of Islam and Muslims (JNIM) have weighed heavily on the Malian economy.

Mali.title: Mali: Military Attacks On Civilians, Insurgent Abuses
Mali.summary: African Union Should Act to Prevent Further Atrocities - Malian armed forces and their allies have since July 2026 responded to mounting attacks by Islamist and separatist armed groups with abusive counterinsurgency operations in central and northern Mali. - The Malian military, armed groups, and insurgent forces are committing grave laws-of-war violations while international organizations and governments largely stand by.

Mali.title: HRW: Malian Army, Rebels Abusing Civilians
Mali.summary: Mali’s military and its Russian allies have killed civilians in violations of international law, while terrorists and separatist fighters have also committed serious abuses, Human Rights Watch (HRW) said on Monday. In a new report, the rights organisation accused the warring parties of violating international humanitarian law and criticised the lack of action by governments and international bodies.

Mali.title: Mali's army and rebel opponents guilty of human rights violations, new report finds
Mali.summary: The Malian army and its Russian paramilitary allies have killed civilians in violation of international law, while their rebel opponents have done likewise, Human Rights Watch (HRW) said on Monday. "The Malian military, armed groups and insurgent forces are committing grave laws-of-war violations while international organisations and governments largely stand by," the rights watchdog said in a new report.

Niger.title: Niger: fuel shortage spreads to capital Niamey
Niger.summary: Niger has been ruled since July 2023 by a military regime that advocates sovereignty, particularly over the country's mineral resources, which is in particular an oil producer. But the national refinery, in Zinder, fails to meet demand. Spared in recent weeks by these shortages, the capital Niamey of two million inhabitants is now affected .
